findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached FLOWR endpoint VJP, so no affinity-head derivative or extra model forward is available as evidence.

The observed learning window is the score-time interval 0.0 to 0.5 with 50 observed score nodes, and the curve support is the same interval; recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior applies, so no absolute affinity label is observable in this packet.

Continuous contrast features over the observed support are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass shows 4 sign changes with a positive first rate and negative last rate, and landmark_00_local_dx shows 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts, so a constant rule is not supported by these curves.

Several landmark local contrast features have large-magnitude first and last rate z-scores of opposite sign (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z strongly negative, last_rate_z positive; landmark_00_local_cyy similar), indicating rate changes within the observed window rather than a single constant rate.

No polynomial fit is accepted for the inspected continuous trends and extrapolation is disallowed, so any time-conditioned rule must be restricted to observed-node interpolation within 0.0-0.5 and cannot be extrapolated.

hypotheses.falsifier: a constant rule matches the observed-node contrast within the reported node RMSE across the window
hypotheses.observable: landmark local contrast features over observed score nodes 0.0-0.5
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast rule that follows the observed sign and rate changes of landmark local features within the observed window will track the contrast better than a constant rule, because the inspected curves show multiple sign changes and opposite-sign first/last rates.

hypotheses.falsifier: whole-window mean of the soft mass shows a stable signed effect consistent with an absolute geometric descriptor
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass whole-window z versus first/last rate z
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_soft_mass contrast is a selection-enrichment descriptor rather than an absolute geometric target, since it is a soft mass over observed selection nodes and its whole-window z is small relative to its endpoint rate z-scores.

limitations: Recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior applies, so no absolute affinity benefit or final-affinity label is observable in the supplied evidence.
No decoded terminal labels or independent outcome evaluation data are supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Only continuous_trends rows were inspected; branch-adjusted, survival, increment, turnover, joint and regional tables were not read, so multiplicity-adjusted ranking and joint-pattern coupling claims are not supported here.
The inspected continuous trends are diagnostic contrast curves, not absolute reward targets, and no registered reward recipe change is asserted by this analysis.
